en: The Sūtra on the Compendium of the True Realm of All Buddhas, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Prajñā of Kaśmīra by Imperial Decree. Chapter One: The Introduction. **Introduction** Thus have I heard. At one time the Bhagavat was dwelling in the great city of Rājagṛha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Kalandaka-nivāpa. There he was accompanied by a great assembly of twelve thousand bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats—free from outflows, free from afflictions, having attained mastery over their minds, like great dragons, like great elephants, having done what was to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their own goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, and whose minds were liberated through perfect knowledge. Also present were eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, all of whom had attained the stage of non-retrogression, possessed the ten powers, and were endowed with the four fearlessnesses. Furthermore, there were the four great kings of the gods, the thirty-three gods, the yāma gods, the tuṣita gods, the nirmāṇarati gods, the paranirmita-vaśavartin gods, the brahmakāyika gods, and so forth, up to the akaniṣṭha gods; and also the four great dragon kings, as well as the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and other celestial beings, humans, and non-humans who had gathered from the ten directions. At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded and honored by this great assembly, sat upon his lion throne. His body was adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary characteristics. He emitted a great light that illuminated the worlds of the ten directions, surpassing the brilliance of the sun, moon, and all the stars and constellations. The entire assembly beheld him with eyes of faith and joy, their bodies and minds filled with serene bliss. Then, the venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him: "World-Honored One, today the Tathāgata’s countenance is more radiant than usual, and the great assembly is filled with joy. For what reason has the Tathāgata manifested such a sublime radiance? May the World-Honored One please explain it for the sake of the great assembly. The Buddha told Ānanda: "Excellent, excellent! You have asked this question well. Listen attentively and bear it in mind; I shall now explain it for you. Ānanda replied: "Yes, World-Honored One, I am eager to hear. The Buddha said: "Ānanda, there is a sūtra called the *Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra* (The Adornment of the Light of Wisdom Entering the Realm of All Buddhas). It is the most profound and supreme among all dharmas, a treasury of the Tathāgatas' secret teachings, and the ultimate destination of all bodhisattvas. It can cause sentient beings to transcend birth and death and attain the state of Buddhahood. Because of this, the Tathāgata has manifested this great light. Ānanda further asked: "World-Honored One, when will the Tathāgata preach this sūtra? The Buddha replied: "In the future, after my parinirvāṇa, when the True Dharma is about to perish and the world is filled with suffering, there will appear a king named *Candraprabha* (Moonlight). He will rule over Jambudvīpa with righteousness and compassion, protecting all sentient beings. At that time, I will entrust this sūtra to him. By the power of his merit and my past vows, he will cause this dharma to be widely propagated throughout the world, benefiting immeasurable beings and leading them to liberation. Having spoken thus, the Buddha entered into a samādhi called *Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatāra*. As soon as he had entered this concentration, his body emitted a vast light that pervaded the ten directions, and from every pore of his skin issued forth hundreds of thousands of koṭis of rays. From each ray emerged countless transformation buddhas, who traveled to the various worlds, preaching this sūtra and liberating sentient beings. When the Buddha arose from this samādhi, the entire great assembly saw these wondrous signs and rejoiced with great faith. The venerable Ānanda once again addressed the Buddha: "World-Honored One, I pray that you will now expound this *Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra-sūtra*, for the sake of the future generations of bodhisattvas and all sentient beings. The Buddha said: "It is well, Ānanda. I shall now speak of this sūtra for the benefit of all. This concludes the first chapter, the Introduction, of the *Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra-sūtra*.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the Buddha, the Bhagavān, had perfectly accomplished the samaya-wisdom of vajra majesty and possessed various rare and most excellent qualities;
he had already attained the precious crown of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas and transcended the three realms.
They have already been able to realize and enter the great yoga method of the wondrous discerning wisdom (*pratyavekṣaṇājñāna*) of all Tathāgatas, attaining unimpeded mastery;

they have already been able to accomplish the subtle wisdom-seals (*jñānamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, skillfully accomplishing all tasks, and satisfying the various aspirations and requests of all sentient beings according to their inclinations.

The Great Compassionate Tathāgata Vairocana is eternally abiding in his essential nature; without beginning and without end, his three karmas are as firm and solid as a vajra. All Buddhas of the ten directions collectively revere him, and all Bodhisattvas pay him homage and offer praise.

At that time, the Bhagavān was dwelling atop Mount Sumeru, within the Palace of Śakra, Lord of the Thirty-three Heavens, in the Mahāmaṇi-uttama-kūṭāgāra (the Supreme Pavilion of Great Jewels)—a place where the Buddhas of the three periods of time constantly preach the Dharma. Its surface was as soft as *tūla* cotton, composed of white jade, with a luster as pure as snow and mother-of-pearl.

There was a magnificent pavilion adorned with the seven precious jewels, with jeweled bells and chimes suspended everywhere; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced subtle and wondrous sounds. It was further embellished with silk canopies, banners, streamers, flower garlands, necklaces, and crescent and full-moon ornaments. Its radiance shone brilliantly throughout the void, and countless celestial beings and rishis all joined in its praise—accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and a retinue of sixteen hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* bodhisattvas.
Their names were:

Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, Bodhisattva Vajracāpa, Bodhisattva Vajrasādhu, Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, Bodhisattva Vajratejas, Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, Bodhisattva Vajrahāsa, Bodhisattva Vajranetra, Bodhisattva Vajradhara, Bodhisattva Vajracakra, Bodhisattva Vajrabhāṣa, Bodhisattva Vajrakarma, Bodhisattva Vajravīrya, Bodhisattva Vajravinardana, and Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi. These sixteen Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas each had a retinue of one hundred billion nayutas of bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, there were four Vajra Goddesses, named:
the Vajra Incense Goddess, the Vajra Flower-scattering Goddess, the Vajra Lamp-lighting Goddess, and the Vajra Perfume-smearing Goddess.
Each of these Vajra goddesses is accompanied by a retinue of one thousand Vajra goddesses.
Furthermore, there are four Vajra deities, named:
Vajrāṅkuśī (Vajra Hook), Vajrapāśī (Vajra Noose), Vajrasphoṭī (Vajra Chain), and Vajraghaṇṭā (Vajra Bell).
Each of these Vajra-devas was accompanied by a retinue of one thousand Vajra-devas.

Furthermore, there were the great celestial kings such as Śakra Devānām Indra, Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, Mahābrahmā, and Maheśvara; as well as innumerable sons of the gods from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and countless koṭis of nayutas of celestial maidens, all offering worship with various songs and dances with single-minded devotion.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless transformation Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, appearing throughout Jambudvīpa and filling the void of space. Each Tathāgata manifested infinite and vast Buddha-fields, and within each of those fields, every Tathāgata was surrounded by an ocean-like assembly of countless Bodhisattvas and holy sages, preaching this Great Dharma.

At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata, who abides eternally and unchangingly throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space, surveyed the ocean-like assembly like a great elephant king and entered the rare Vajra Samādhi of the wisdom of the enlightened nature that pervades all of empty space.
Having entered samādhi, he emitted a blue light from his chest that illuminated immeasurable worlds in the eastern direction like deep-blue lapis lazuli.

From his face down to his toes, a blue light issued from every single pore; these lights merged into a single color, pervading everywhere—reaching downward as far as the Avīci Hell and upward as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
In those worlds, there are immeasurable transformation Buddhas, each of whom manifests boundless and vast Buddha-fields.
Within those Buddha-fields, each Tathāgata is surrounded by a great assembly of Bodhisattvas as numerous as an ocean, who proclaim this Great Dharma.

All sentient beings in the world of darkness, where there is neither sun nor moon—even those born blind—were all illuminated by this light; they beheld all the transformation Buddhas of Vairocana Tathāgata, forever exhausted all suffering and attained immeasurable bliss.
At that time, the Tathāgata, having arisen from meditative concentration, again entered the Great Jewel Samādhi of the Birth of Vajra Splendor, which is as numerous as all the atoms in empty space.
Having entered into samādhi, he emitted golden light from his right shoulder, illuminating immeasurable worlds in the southern direction.

From the crown of his head down to his feet, he emitted this radiance from every single pore; these lights merged into a single color, illuminating the south so that there was nowhere it did not pervade.
In those various worlds, immeasurable transformation Buddhas appear, and those Buddhas manifest boundless and vast Buddha-fields.
In each of those Buddha-fields, every Tathāgata is surrounded by a great assembly of Bodhisattvas as vast as an ocean, and they preach this Great Dharma.

All sentient beings in the world of darkness, where there is neither sun nor moon—even those born blind—were all illumined by this light; they beheld Vairocana Tathāgata and his emanation-buddhas, whereby all their sufferings were eliminated and they experienced immeasurable bliss.
At that time, the Tathāgata arose from meditative concentration and again entered the Samādhi of the Lotus of the Innately Pure Essential Nature of All Dharmas of All Tathāgatas.

Having entered this samādhi, he emitted light the color of a red lotus from his back, illuminating immeasurable worlds in the western direction; furthermore, from all his pores he emitted light the color of a red lotus, universally illuminating the western direction until the entire realm of empty space was merged into a single color, pervading everywhere without exception.
In those worlds, there are immeasurable emanation buddhas, and those emanation buddhas manifest unspeakably vast buddha-fields.
In each of those buddha-fields, every Tathāgata is surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas as numerous as an infinite and boundless ocean, and they proclaim this Great Dharma.

All sentient beings in the world of darkness, where there is neither sun nor moon—even those born blind—were all illumined by this light; they beheld Vairocana Tathāgata and all the Buddhas, whereby their manifold sufferings were forever extinguished and they experienced immeasurable bliss.

At that time, the Tathāgata arose from this samādhi and again entered the samādhi of the various activities of the supreme accomplishment of the unerring, firm, and adamantine Great Bodhi of all Tathāgatas.
Having entered samādhi, he emitted five-colored light from his left shoulder, illuminating immeasurable worlds in the north.

From all parts of his body, even down to his pores, he emitted five-colored light that filled the northern direction, pervading the entire realm of empty space until it merged into a single color, reaching everywhere without exception.
In those various worlds, immeasurable transformation Buddhas and those Tathāgatas manifest inconceivable and vast Buddha-fields.
In each of those Buddha-fields, every Tathāgata is surrounded by a great assembly of Bodhisattvas as vast as an ocean, and they preach this Great Dharma.

All sentient beings in the world of darkness, where there is neither sun nor moon—even those born blind—were all illumined by this light, enabling them to see Vairocana Tathāgata and all the Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions; these beings were forever freed from all suffering and came to experience immeasurable bliss.

At that time, the Tathāgata arose from this samādhi and again entered the most supreme samādhi called "Pervading All Limits of Space, Manifesting All Objective Wisdom, Capable of Skillfully Subduing the Entire Realm of Sentient Beings."

Having entered samādhi, he emitted white light from the crown of his head, which illuminated all buddha-fields throughout the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions, pervading them all without exception.
The four kinds of light rays previously emitted came from the four directions and entered within this light, filling the entirety of space.
Buddhas and bodhisattvas as numerous as motes of dust and sands, along with boundless hosts of devas, beheld this radiance and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence, each thinking:
"By what causes and conditions has this auspicious sign been manifested?"

At that time, the Buddha Bhagavān—the Great Holy Lord who is tranquil and without beginning or end, the Supreme Great Sage who protects sentient beings, the guardian of the world who benefits all living beings, acting as a father and mother to them, uprooting the suffering of birth and death, possessing great skillful means and supreme peace and happiness, endowed with great kindness and compassion and the knowledge of others' minds—the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, observing the doubts in the minds of the great assembly, addressed all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas in the gathering, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well."

I now expound the *Mahāyoga-sarvabuddha-rahasya-cittabhūmi-dharmaparyāya-tathāgata-viṣaya-saṃgraha-bhūtārtha-sūtra*, to forever sever all the nets of doubt within you; by practicing this dharma alone, one attains the path to Buddhahood.
This Dharma is well able to lead all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas to sit beneath the Bodhi tree;
this Dharma is the very root of all Buddhas; this Dharma can extinguish all evil karma; this Dharma can fulfill all aspirations;
and this Dharma can exhaust all the suffering of birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, and pain for all sentient beings.
The ocean: this Dharma can cross the wilderness of birth and death; this Dharma can still the waves of birth and death.
This Dharma is the seed of all Buddhas; this Dharma is the erection of the great Dharma-banner;
this Dharma is the great lion throne; this Dharma is the unsurpassed Wheel of the Dharma; this Dharma is...
This great torch of wisdom can illuminate the darkness of the long night of birth and death; this Dharma is the blowing of the great Dharma-conch,
this Dharma is the beating of the great Dharma-drum, and this Dharma is the great lion’s roar that can destroy the heterodox paths.
At that time, in the great assembly, there were immeasurable and boundless emanation buddhas, sixteen koṭi-nayuta bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, Śakra-devānām-indra, Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven;
Mahābrahmā, Lord of the Sahā World; Suyāma-devaputra; Tuṣita-devaputra; and Nirmāṇarati-devaputra...
The Transformation Deva King, the Sovereign Deva King, and countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of koṭi-nayuta devas from other worlds,
standing in the presence of the Buddha, heard the title of the *Sūtra on the Compendium of the Secrets of All Buddhas:
The Mahāyāna Abhidharma of the Great Yoga concerning the Realm of All Buddhas*, and were filled with joy.

They leaped for joy, having attained what they had never experienced before; their hearts were filled with love and delight, and each removed the celestial robes they were wearing, holding them in their hands as they whirled through the air in offering to the Buddha.

They also made offerings to the Buddhas and the great assemblies with celestial *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, and *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers; furthermore, they offered hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of exquisite celestial music from the midst of the sky to the Buddhas; and they rained down various kinds of exquisite celestial flowers—namely, *campaka* flowers, *sumana* flowers, *atimuktaka* flowers, *pāriyātraka* flowers, and so forth—to make offerings to the Buddhas and the great assemblies.

At that time, when the great assembly heard the name of this sutra, immeasurable sentient beings attained great benefit; sentient beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Radiance (*prabhākārī-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arciṣmatī-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Far-Going (*dūraṃgamā-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*); some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of Good Wisdom (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*); and some bodhisattvas attained the Stage of the Dharma Cloud (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*). Furthermore, immeasurable and boundless sons of the gods and others resolved their minds on enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), never to regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Chapter Two: The Chapter on Birth At that time, the Buddha, the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, dwelt in the mind of Samantabhadra. Upon his crown, a jeweled tiara manifested inconceivable phenomena, within which the reflections of all emanation-buddhas appeared. These Tathāgatas are the Great Avalokiteśvaras who have attained the perfection of great dharma-wisdom; they possess the unerring and unobstructed *viṣkambha-karma* of all Tathāgatas, are skillful in all activities to be performed, and there is no wish of theirs that remains unfulfilled. Relying upon great supernormal power, the essence of all Buddhas is established within their own hearts, adorning their Dharma-bodies.

At that time, the Tathāgata entered the samādhi called "The Vast Majestic Power of Vajrasattva Born from the Samaya of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva of All Buddhas. Having arisen from that meditative absorption, he brought forth from his own heart this secret mantra, saying:

“Oṃ vajrasattva. At that time, when Vairocana Tathāgata spoke this Secret Mind-Ground Dharma of the True Yoga of the Realm of All Buddhas, the immeasurable and boundless buddha-fields of the ten directions shook in six ways; even the supreme pavilion of great maṇi jewels in the palace of Śakra, Lord of the Thirty-three on the summit of Mount Sumeru, shook as well. The heavens rained down mandārava flowers, mahāmandārava flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers, and mahāmañjūṣaka flowers, scattering them over the Buddha and the great assembly.

At that time, the great assembly saw these buddha-fields of the ten directions—immeasurable, innumerable, and as many as the sands of the Ganges—tremble in six ways, and they also saw the Great Māṇi Jewel Pavilion of Supreme Excellence within Śakra’s palace atop Mount Sumeru tremble in six ways. They then thought:
"The Tathāgata is now manifesting a great supernatural transformation; by what causes and conditions does this auspicious omen appear?"
At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the great assembly, addressed them, saying:
"Do not give rise to doubt or confusion regarding this. I have now expounded this profound and wondrous Dharma—the very heart within the hearts of all Buddhas of the three periods of time."

All Buddha-dharmas are subsumed within this sūtra, and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sūtra. This teaching is named "The Subtle Abhidharma of Mahāyāna Yoga: The True Realm of All Tathāgatas. It is the most supreme secret of the Vajra-mantras, the heart-essence of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, once this Dharma had issued forth from the hearts of all the Buddhas, the Bhagavat Samantabhadra-dhāraṇī—this secret Dharma—immediately transformed into immeasurable and innumerable perfect lunar discs. These full lunar discs were able to cause the great bodhicitta of all sentient beings to become completely pure.

These countless, perfectly full moon discs are situated to the left and right of all the Tathāgatas; from these moon discs, there manifest the immeasurable and innumerable great wisdom-vajras of all the Tathāgatas.

This great wisdom-vajra emerged from the full moon and re-entered the heart of the Tathāgata Vairocana. By the power of the wondrous and firm samādhi of Vajrasattva and the great majestic power of all the Tathāgatas, immeasurable and innumerable wisdom-vajras merged into a single mass, equal in extent to space, manifesting a great garland of light.

Thus, that garland of light immediately transformed into the five-pronged vajra of the firm wisdom-nature of the sublime body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas; emerging from the hearts of all Buddhas, it came to rest within the palms of the hands of the Tathāgata Vairocana.
From this vajra, various colored lights and vajra forms emerged; immeasurable and innumerable rays of light filled all worlds, equal and unimpeded.

This vajra-light again issued from his mouth, manifesting as the unimpeded dharma-bodies of all Tathāgatas, equal in number to the atoms within the worlds of the ten directions, pervading the ocean of the dharma-realm.
By what causes and conditions is it pervaded throughout the Dharma-realm?

It is because all Tathāgatas have attained equal wisdom and great supernormal powers, manifesting the ability to awaken all sentient beings and cause them to resolve upon the unsurpassed, great Bodhicitta; they are well able to accomplish the various inconceivable and wondrous practices of Samantabhadra; through the power of the causal lineage of all Tathāgatas, they are well able to approach, revere, and make offerings to the Great Bodhi Tree; they are able to subdue all evil Māras Pāpīyas; they realize great Bodhi; they are able to awaken themselves and turn the unsurpassed, most wondrous Wheel of Dharma; and they are even able to protect all sentient beings throughout the entirety of space, performing every kind of benefit and peace.

All Tathāgatas are well able to accomplish the supreme siddhi of great wisdom and supernormal powers; all Tathāgatas are well able to manifest various kinds of supernormal powers. By virtue of the essence of Samantabhadra-samādhi and the subtle, firm, and harmonious power of Vajra-samādhi, the body of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra appears.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, standing within the heart of Vairocana Tathāgata, spoke these verses:
“Excellent! Rare indeed am I, Samantabhadra, Whose wondrous body is firm and of true nature.
By the power of this firmness, though formless, I manifest a birth-body for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.”

At that time, the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra emerged from the heart of Vairocana Tathāgata and sat before all the Buddhas within a moon disc, holding a vajra in his right hand and rotating it within his palm.

At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata entered the Great Samaya Samādhi of the Unbreakable Vajra Wisdom of All Tathāgatas. By the power of this samādhi, for the sake of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, he manifested the Great Samaya of the Wisdom of Great Expedient Means and Power, which brings benefit to sentient beings through the subtle Great Dharma Wheel of the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Buddhas. It provides protection for all, including all sovereign lords throughout the entire realm of sentient beings, and is deeply cherished by those with hearts of great peace and bliss; it further encompasses such fruits as the Wisdom of Equality of all Tathāgatas, supreme supernatural powers, the Abhidharma of the Mahāyāna, and the most excellent siddhis.

This is the Vajra of the Siddhi of all Tathāgatas; because he wishes to bestow it upon the hand of the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, because he wishes to bestow the essence of the Universal Monarch (Cakravartin) of all Tathāgatas, because he wishes to bestow the inconceivable Buddha-activities of all Tathāgatas, and because he wishes to bestow the consecration of the jeweled crown and white silk, the Tathāgata Vairocana bestowed the Vajra-seal with his own two hands.
Then all the Tathāgatas conferred upon him the name-consecration, bestowing the title Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having obtained this vajra, held the vajra-pestle in his right hand, rotated it within his palm, placed it at his heart, and spoke these verses:
“This is the supreme vajra-mahāsiddhi of all the Tathāgatas.”
"The Buddhas place their two hands upon me; The signless manifests signs for the benefit of living beings. Chapter Three:

The Great Maṇḍala of the Vajra Realm From the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha*, the Scripture on the Comprehension of the Real Sphere of All Buddhas. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, sustained by the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, surveyed all sentient beings throughout the infinite, boundless worlds of the ten directions—as numerous as the atoms of dust—as clearly as one would view an *āmala* fruit in the palm of one's hand. For the sake of these sentient beings, he gave rise to a heart of great compassion. He immediately rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

Among all sentient beings in the world, some are attached to wealth and treasures; some are attached to food and drink; some are attached to the five desires and harbor hatred toward the Triple Gem; and some delight in singing, dancing, and unrestrained play. Such beings have never seen or heard the true and wondrous Dharma; they enter into the teachings of heterodox paths and false views, and do not cultivate the brahma-conduct of the Buddhas.

Those sentient beings have extensively committed evil deeds and created the causes for the hells; no other dharmas whatsoever can deliver them, but only the supreme Great Dharma of the Vajradhātu Mahāmaṇḍala is well able to provide protection and salvation.

Why is this? If there are sentient beings who commit various kinds of transgressions and are destined to fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, or the eight difficult conditions, only this Dharma is capable of delivering them.
If there are sentient beings who aspire to all supreme peace and happiness, only this secret [teaching] can perfectly fulfill them.

Furthermore, for those sentient beings who delight in the True Dharma and seek the pure precepts, samādhis, wisdom, and the most excellent siddhi of all Tathāgatas, this secret dharma serves as the practice of skillful means.

Those who have cultivated various practices under many Buddhas in pursuit of fruits such as meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and liberation (*vimukti*)—such sentient beings can easily enter this maṇḍala and immediately realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; how much more so, then, the worldly fruits of merit and happiness?
"Now, the World-Honored One has given rise to the most supreme mind of great compassion for these matters; you shall now expound the dharma of the dhāraṇī.
At that time, the Buddha, the Bhagavān, addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
Vajrapāṇi! It is so, it is so, just as you have said.
Arising with great compassion, demonstrate the path of reality for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages.
"Good son! Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this well; I shall now explain for you in successive order the Dharma of this great maṇḍala path."
“Good son! If there are those who practice and study this Great Maṇḍala Dharma of the Yoga of the Vajradhātu, which is the realm of all Buddhas, what is the very first thing they should do?”

When a practitioner of yoga first enters the maṇḍala, they should first form the mudrā for the extinction of transgressions: interlace the tips of the left and right thumbs with the index fingers; extend the middle fingers of both hands straight upward; then bend the tips of the two middle fingers against each other so that they rest upon the ring fingers of the left and right respectively; and let the little fingers be as the thumbs and index fingers are interlaced. Thereupon, one should recite the mantra.
Thus, these are called the secret mantras of the three karmas, which are:
“Oṃ sarvabāśuddha-svabhāva-śuddhaḥ svāhā. Having recited this once, one should form this thought: “The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure;
myself and all sentient beings are also pure by intrinsic nature.”

Having formed this visualization, furthermore, the yoga practitioner binds the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā (*vajra-añjali-mudrā*). First, join the two palms; next, interlace the ten fingertips with the right pressing over the left. This is the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā, from which all mudrās arise.

The mantra is recited as: “Oṃ vajra-jvala. Having recited the mantra, one seals the five places of the body: first, the crown of the head; second, the right shoulder; third, the left shoulder; fourth, the heart; and fifth, the throat.
At that time, the practitioner empowers the five locations with this Vajra-joined-palms mudrā; immediately, the vajra armor is donned upon their bodies.
The practitioner and the disciple become firm in body and mind, attaining complete security, such that no malevolent spirits or vināyakas can find an opportunity to harm them.

"Furthermore, the practitioner of yoga forms the Vajra-bond mudrā (Vajrabandha-mudrā). Without releasing the preceding Vajra-palms mudrā (Vajra-añjali-mudrā), the ten fingers of the left and right hands are interlaced: the five fingers of the right hand firmly grasp the left hand, and the five fingers of the left hand firmly grasp the right hand, in the manner of being bound together."
The mantra is recited as follows:

Oṃ vajra-maṇḍala taṭṭa. Recite the final three syllables three times with emphasis; for each repetition of these three syllables, extend the middle fingers of both hands straight upward and snap the fingers once, repeating this three times.
At that time, having held the mantra, the practitioner should form this visualization:

"All afflictions within my own body and the bodies of all sentient beings are completely extinguished; both internally and externally they are pure like space, becoming a fit dwelling place for all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. All Vināyakas, spirits, and ghosts are entirely driven away. The four means of attraction, the ten wholesome actions, the ten pāramitās, and all virtuous deeds are fully perfected, just as the myriad rivers flow into the great ocean."

Having formed this thought, furthermore, the practitioner of yoga, about to enter the maṇḍala, places both knees upon the ground, joins his palms in prostration, and performs the mudrā of awakening-arising.

First, form the vajra-fist; next, interlace the little fingers of the left and right hands, hooking the right over the left. Then, extend the index fingers of both hands so that their tips touch, and form this visualization:

"Just as the Tathāgata Vairocana now commands the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and assemblies of sages and worthies, numbering as the atoms and sands of the worlds of the ten directions, to cease all activities such as entering samādhi or preaching the Dharma, and to assemble at this site of practice to observe the practitioner and together receive and benefit all sentient beings."
Having performed this visualization, one forms the *udvīkṣaṇa-mudrā* (the upward-facing seal) and recites the mantra:

"Oṃ vajraṭṭha. Furthermore, the practitioner of yoga forms the *vajramuṣṭi-mudrā* (the adamantine fist seal): first, place the left fist at the heart; next, extend the right fist outward; then, extend the index finger of the left fist, and again extend the index finger of the right fist outward.
The mantra is: HŪṂ. Reciting this mantra once, one should immediately form this visualization:
"Expel all Vināyakas and all evil spirits and ghosts within my body and inside the maṇḍala."
When the practitioner holds this mantra, they should move their right fist with the index finger pointing outward; this is the gesture of expulsion, known as the "Dispatching" mudrā.

Once the māras and others have been expelled, the yoga practitioner next forms the Vajra Hook seal (*vajrāṅkuśa-mudrā*): first forming the Vajra Bond seal (*vajrabandha-mudrā*), then extending the index finger of the right hand and slightly bending it, visualizing it as a hook seal to invite all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of noble ones.
The mantra is recited as follows:
"Oṃ vajra-guhyaka-jña. As soon as this mantra is held, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy assemblies descend.

"Furthermore, the practitioner of yoga forms the *saṃnipāta-mudrā*: first, he forms the vajra-fist with both hands; next, he places the left fist upon his right knee; then, he crosses his arms over his chest with the right fist, binding his heart, and immediately forms this thought:
'All the Tathāgatas, Bodhisattvas, and noble assemblies have gathered together.'"
Having performed this visualization, one recites the mantra:
*Oṃ vajrasamāja*. Having recited this mantra, one immediately forms this thought:
"Since the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have already assembled, they give rise to a heart of joy."
"Without shaking the two arms, one should snap the fingers three times with the tips of the thumbs and index fingers of both hands.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke these verses:
"The two wings of concentration and wisdom, the vajra-fists, Crossed arms and bound heart through the power of diligence."
A snap of the fingers sends forth sound throughout the entire Dharma-realm; Contemplate this with clarity and universally invite all Tathāgatas.
